articles.description:
This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path One: Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content
On 1 November 2026, Canada stops changing its clocks — one province at a time. British Columbia, Alberta and the Northwest Territories already went permanent this year; Manitoba follows on 31 October. IANA shipped five tzdata releases in 2026 to keep up, and for several of these changes it deliberately models the switch on 1 November at 02:00 instead of the legal date (a documented "temporary hack"). Morocco quietly went back to GMT on 20 September.
Meanwhile, the Node.js you're running ships whatever tz data it was built with. On my machine that's 2025b: 11 of 597 zones are wrong in 2026–27. Even the Vercel runtime this project is deployed on (tzdata 2026c) still puts Winnipeg an hour off. Ask…

articles.author: Terminal Chai
articles.description:
Autonomous web agents represent one of the most promising frontiers of modern artificial intelligence. However, developers who have deployed browser agents in production quickly encounter a severe constraint: excessive latency and prohibitive token costs.

The prevailing industry pattern—often referred to as "Computer Use" or vision-based browsing—relies on a brute-force approach:
Render the browser viewport to a full-resolution PNG image.
Send image buffers across the network to a frontier multimodal model.
Wait several seconds for the model to predict spatial $(x, y)$ coordinate clicks.
Execute the click, wait for page mutations, and repeat the cycle.
On realistic web tasks (such as searching travel portals or completing multi-step checkouts), this loop frequently requires 60 to 120 seco…
articles.title: Jev Ultrafast: The Sub-10-Second Web Agent Architecture

articles.author: Shourya Shinde
articles.description:
This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend
StudyMate is an AI-powered study companion built for students who spend too much time converting long study material into something they can actually revise.
I built it with fellow students in mind — especially when exams are approaching and there is a lot of material to go through.
StudyMate allows a student to paste their study material and automatically generates:
📝 Concise study notes
🔑 Important key points
🧠 AI-generated multiple-choice questions
✅ Interactive quizzes with instant scoring
Instead of manually reading through lengthy material and creating revision notes and questions, StudyMate turns the material into a structured revision experience in seconds.




💻 GitHub Repository: https://github.com/ShouryaShinde/StudyMate
The project is organized as a monorepo containing:
client/ — React + Vite frontend
packages/ui/ — Shared shadcn/ui components
server/ — Node.js + Express backend
Ollama integration for local AI inference
StudyMate is built around open-source AI and local inference.
Frontend
React
TypeScript
Vite
Tailwind CSS
shadcn/ui
React Router
Backend
Node.js
Express.js
Ollama
AI Model
llama3.2:3b
The core AI functionality runs through Ollama locally rather than relying on a proprietary hosted AI API.
When a student submits study material, the frontend sends it to the Express backend:
Student
   ↓
Study Material
   ↓
React Frontend
   ↓
Express API
   ↓
Ollama
   ↓
Llama 3.2 3B
   ↓
Structured JSON
   ↓
Notes + Key Points + Quiz
articles.title: DEV Challenge 1 Complete - StudyMate

Product Security problems in startups are rarely caused by a complete absence of security. More often, security exists — but it grew organically, unevenly, and without a clear operating model.
Over time, I reviewed a sample of 15 anonymized Product Security engagements across startups, scale-ups, and growing software companies.
The environments were different. So were the architectures, cloud platforms, engineering maturity, and business constraints.
But the same patterns kept appearing.
This is not intended to be an industry benchmark. The sample is small, the percentages are rounded, and the observations are directional. What makes the data useful is not statistical significance — it is the recurrence of the same practical problems across different teams.

articles.description:
This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path Two: Vibe-Code Something Strange
Labs run on numbers that reputable sources can't agree on. How long should 1:10 bleach sit on a spill? The University of Washington says 30 minutes, UC Santa Barbara 20, Case Western 15–20. How long do you autoclave biohazardous waste? Virginia Tech says 30 minutes; UNC says 60.
Someone in every lab eventually decides, and the decision usually lives in a PI's head or a laminated sheet nobody can find.
Bench Court puts those disagreements on trial.
Every disputed value in my protocol dataset becomes a case, named the way the law would name it: Case Western Reserve University v. University of Washington (bleach contact time).
An agent, the clerk, reads every claim about that parameter, opens the case through…
